name: Kalman Local-Linear-Trend Slope t-Statistic
note: A two-state local-linear-trend Kalman filter on log close, with the per-bar observation noise set by the Parkinson range estimator so the filter automatically distrusts wide-range bars and trusts narrow ones. The signal is a SIGNIFICANCE TEST, not a level or a crossover: enter when the posterior drift crosses t_in of its own estimated standard errors, which needs no per-symbol retuning. Rbar is a TRAILING mean of the Parkinson variance so the filter stays causal.
source: Andrew Harvey, 'Forecasting, Structural Time Series Models and the Kalman Filter' (Cambridge University Press, 1989), the local linear trend model and its filtering recursions; M. Parkinson, 'The Extreme Value Method for Estimating the Variance of the Rate of Return', Journal of Business 53(1), 1980, pp. 61-65. Combining the two and trading the slope t-statistic is the harvester's synthesis.
code:
import math


def family_init(ctx):
    b = ctx.bars
    n = len(b)
    four_ln2 = 4.0 * math.log(2.0)
    R = [1e-8] * n
    for j in range(n):
        h = float(b[j]["h"])
        l = float(b[j]["l"])
        if h > 0.0 and l > 0.0 and h > l:
            r = math.log(h / l) ** 2 / four_ln2
            if r > 1e-8:
                R[j] = r
    w = int(ctx.p.rbar_n)
    if w < 2:
        w = 2
    rbar = [0.0] * n
    run = 0.0
    for j in range(n):
        run += R[j]
        if j >= w:
            run -= R[j - w]
        rbar[j] = run / (j + 1 if j + 1 < w else w)
    k1 = float(ctx.p.k1)
    k2 = float(ctx.p.k2)
    t = [None] * n
    bser = [None] * n
    mu = math.log(max(float(b[0]["c"]), 1e-9))
    be = 0.0
    p11 = rbar[0]
    p12 = 0.0
    p21 = 0.0
    p22 = rbar[0] / 100.0
    for j in range(n):
        if j > 0:
            q1 = k1 * rbar[j]
            q2 = k2 * rbar[j]
            mu = mu + be
            a11 = p11 + p12 + p21 + p22 + q1
            a12 = p12 + p22
            a21 = p21 + p22
            a22 = p22 + q2
            y = math.log(max(float(b[j]["c"]), 1e-9))
            s = a11 + R[j]
            if s <= 0.0:
                s = 1e-12
            g1 = a11 / s
            g2 = a21 / s
            innov = y - mu
            mu = mu + g1 * innov
            be = be + g2 * innov
            p11 = (1.0 - g1) * a11
            p12 = (1.0 - g1) * a12
            p21 = a21 - g2 * a11
            p22 = a22 - g2 * a12
        bser[j] = be
        if p22 > 0.0:
            t[j] = be / (p22 ** 0.5)
    ctx.tstat = ctx.series(t, "kalman_t")
    ctx.beta = ctx.series(bser, "kalman_beta")


def signal(ctx, i):
    if i < 2:
        return 0
    t = ctx.tstat[i]
    pt = ctx.tstat[i - 1]
    if t is None or pt is None:
        return 0
    thr = float(ctx.p.t_in)
    if t > thr and pt <= thr:
        return 1
    if t < -thr and pt >= -thr:
        return -1
    return 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    t = ctx.tstat[i]
    be = ctx.beta[i]
    if t is None or be is None:
        return False
    out = float(ctx.p.t_out)
    if ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long":
        return t < out or be < 0.0
    return t > -out or be > 0.0
